dimensions.assessment: Affects organizations and entities that post cash bond or bail for defendants, such as charitable bail funds.
dimensions.evidence: entities and organizations that pay cash bond or bail for defendants (e.g., charitable bail funds) are engaged in the business of insurance

dimensions.assessment: Subjects previously excluded entities to federal criminal provisions for insurance fraud and state regulatory licensing.
dimensions.evidence: subject to federal criminal provisions related to insurance fraud, as well as state licensing requirements and regulation by state insurance commissions.

dimensions.assessment: Potential economic and compliance effects on bail-paying entities, but no direct federal spending figures are provided.
Amends federal criminal code regarding insurance fraud definitions.
dimensions.evidence: Section 1033(f)(1)(A) of title 18, United States Code, is amended by inserting before the comma the following: '(including the posting of monetary bail...)'

dimensions.assessment: Permanent change to federal criminal law and regulatory jurisdiction.

missing_information: The exact number of organizations or funds that will be reclassified under the new definition.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill broadens the definition of the business of insurance under federal law to include posting bail and bonds, subjecting charitable bail funds and similar entities to insurance fraud provisions and state regulation.
